deadline.value: The Graduate School's preferred date for international Fall applicants is July 1. The page says some programs have earlier deadlines, and none was found for this program.

gre_subject.value: No subject GRE applies to engineering.

gre_general.value: A GRE score is required by the College of Engineering and Science, but the requirement may be waived for exceptionally qualified students.
gre_general.quote: An official Graduate Record Examination (GRE) score is required for admission, but this requirement may be waived for exceptionally qualified students

supervisor.value: Students select a research advisor during their first term, so an advisor's agreement is not a condition of admission.
supervisor.quote: During the first term, students are required to select (by mutal consent) a research advisor (Major Advisor)

funding.value: Funding comes from a limited number of graduate assistantships, so it is not guaranteed.
funding.quote: Financial assistance is available to qualified graduate students in the form of a limited number of graduate assistantships

entry_route.value: The page sets 66 hours beyond the bachelor's degree but does not say whether a master's is needed.
entry_route.quote: Students in this program are expected to complete 66 graduate hours (including dissertation) beyond the baccalaureate degree

notes: One PhD in Engineering with five concentrations: Cyberspace, Engineering Education, Engineering Physics, Materials and Infrastructure Systems, Micro and Nanoscale Systems. Primary field is materials; physics and civil come from the Engineering Physics and Infrastructure concentrations. The catalog entry does not name each engineering discipline. The COES page mentions a Chemical Engineering PhD student, but no chemical engineering PhD is listed.
name: PhD in Engineering
